Source code for shatranj.main

"""
main.py - Entry point of the Shatranj program

Role: Handles command-line options (F1, F4 of the specifications)
      and then launches the appropriate interface (CLI by default).

Why argparse?
  The specifications (section 1.12) require argparse for Python.
  argparse automatically handles -h/--help and error messages.

Supported options (F1):
  -h / --help     : show help
  -V / --version  : show version
  -v / --verbose  : verbose mode
  -d / --debug    : debug mode
  -b / --blitz    : blitz mode (F5)
  -t / --time     : time in minutes for blitz (F5)
  -g / --gui      : graphical interface (F7) - not yet implemented
  -a / --ai       : AI player (F8) - not yet implemented
"""

import argparse
import sys

# Program version
VERSION = "0.1.0"




[docs]
def build_argument_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """
    Builds and returns the argument parser.

    Separating parser construction from usage
    makes unit testing easier.
    """
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="shatranj",
        description="Shatranj - Indian Chess game",
        # Epilog displayed after the options list in --help
        epilog="Examples:\n"
               "  shatranj              Start a new game (CLI)\n"
               "  shatranj -b -t 15    Start a blitz game (15 min per player)\n"
               "  shatranj save.shatranj  Resume a saved game\n",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )

    # -V / --version : show version and exit (F1)
    parser.add_argument(
        "-V", "--version",
        action="version",
        version=f"%(prog)s {VERSION}",
    )

    # -v / --verbose : increase verbosity (F1)
    parser.add_argument(
        "-v", "--verbose",
        action="store_true",
        default=False,
        help="Increase verbosity",
    )

    # -d / --debug : enable debug messages (F1)
    parser.add_argument(
        "-d", "--debug",
        action="store_true",
        default=False,
        help="Enable debug messages",
    )

    # -b / --blitz : blitz mode (F5)
    parser.add_argument(
        "-b", "--blitz",
        action="store_true",
        default=False,
        help="Start a blitz game (timed)",
    )

    # -t / --time : time limit in minutes for blitz (F5)
    parser.add_argument(
        "-t", "--time",
        type=int,
        default=30,
        metavar="TIME",
        help="Time limit in minutes for blitz mode (default: 30)",
    )

    # -g / --gui : graphical interface (F7)
    parser.add_argument(
        "-g", "--gui",
        action="store_true",
        default=False,
        help="Launch the graphical interface (not yet implemented)",
    )

    # -a / --ai : AI player (F8)
    # nargs="?" means: optional, may have one value
    parser.add_argument(
        "-a", "--ai",
        nargs="?",           
        const="black",       # value if -a is given without argument
        default=None,        # value if -a is absent
        metavar="COLOR",
        help="Replace player COLOR with AI (default: black). "
             "Colors: white, black, all",
    )

    # -c / --contest : contest mode (F6)
    parser.add_argument(
        "-c", "--contest",
        action="store_true",
        default=False,
        help="Contest mode: read a position from a file and output the best move",
    )

    # Optional positional argument: save file (F4)
    parser.add_argument(
        "savefile",
        nargs="?",           
        default=None,
        metavar="SAVEFILE",
        help="Save file to load at startup",
    )

    return parser






[docs]
def main() -> int:
    """
    Main entry point.

    Returns 0 on success, 1 on error (F1).
    """
    parser = build_argument_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args()

    # --- Option validation ---

    # F5: -t without -b prints a warning
    # (check if --time was explicitly given)
    time_given_explicitly = "--time" in sys.argv or "-t" in sys.argv
    if time_given_explicitly and not args.blitz:
        print(
            "Warning: --time is ignored without --blitz (-b).",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

    # --- Launch the interface ---

    if args.gui:
        # Graphical interface (F7) 
        from shatranj.presentation.gui.app import run_gui
        return run_gui()

    # Default: CLI interface
    # Import here to avoid circular imports
    from shatranj.presentation.cli.cli import CLI

    cli = CLI(verbose=args.verbose, debug=args.debug)

    # If a save file is provided, automatically load it (F4)
    if args.savefile:
        # Simulate the command "load FILE"
        cli._do_load([args.savefile])

    # Run the interactive loop
    cli.run()

    return 0




if __name__ == "__main__":
    # sys.exit() converts the int return code to the process exit code
    sys.exit(main())
